use_when: re-saving many scenes, sweeping resources, mass import fixes, generating .tres assets, long bakes that should not block the live editor
"re-save every scene after the engine upgrade"
"fix the import settings on all 200 textures"

resources.summary: Run a GDScript `func run(ctx):` inside the live editor against the open scene — one script instead of a chain of add-node/set-prop calls.
use_when: a change needs 3+ related ops or any computed placement (scatter, grids, procedural meshes, bulk edits)
the ctx helpers (add_node, add_mesh, grid, scatter, light rig, environment) fit the job

resources.summary: Drive and read animation in the RUNNING game — AnimationPlayer clips, AnimationTree state machines, and live Skeleton3D bone poses.
use_when: checking which clip or state-machine state is actually playing in the running game, then driving it (play, seek, travel, set a blend parameter)
"which animation is the player in right now?" / "travel the state machine to Attack and see if it blends"
reading live bone poses to prove a rig moves or an IK target lands

resources.summary: Call one method on a node in the RUNNING game and get its return value — trigger gameplay code directly instead of waiting for input or timers.
use_when: triggering gameplay code in the running game and reading its answer — take_damage, start_wave, get_velocity
"call take_damage(25) on the boss in the running game" / "what does get_velocity return right now?"
a method's result is the fact you need and no property exposes it

resources.summary: Set one property on a node in the RUNNING game — the live object, never the scene file — and read back whether it applied.
use_when: putting the running game into a test state without playing there by hand — teleport the player, set health to 1, flip a flag, toggle visibility
"move the player to (0, 2, 0) in the running game" / "set the boss health to 1 while it is running"
a runtime experiment whose change should die with the run instead of landing in the scene file

resources.summary: Spawn a PackedScene into the RUNNING game (action spawn) or free a live node (action free) — stage a test in seconds without touching the scene file.
use_when: staging a runtime test — place three goblins under the spawner, add a pickup next to the player, remove the boss to test the empty-arena path
"spawn a goblin at (4, 0, -2) in the running game" / "delete that projectile while the game runs"
the spawned or freed node must exist only for this run

resources.summary: Save an explicit scene to disk, for standalone saves or save-as.
use_when: a standalone save or save-as is needed
"save a copy of this scene as level1_backup.tscn"
the user explicitly asks to save

resources.summary: Capture a frame from the editor viewport, an offscreen scene render (fixed or bookmarked pose, numbered labels), or the running game, as an actual image.
use_when: visually verifying layout, scale, framing, or runtime state
"show me what the scene looks like right now"
"did the model land where I put it?" / "does the UI overlap?"
"take a screenshot of the game" / "screenshot the running game" — target "game" grabs the live frame
before/after frames from the SAME viewpoint (framing "bookmark" / "free"), or an annotated screenshot with numbered labels mapped to node paths (marks)

resources.summary: Search the Summer asset library and your own assets by keyword and meaning; returns names, types, preview and import-ready URLs.
use_when: finding an existing asset in the public library before generating a new one
locating a user's generated or uploaded asset by description

resources.summary: Search the Summer library by describing the task in plain words — ranked entries of every kind, with the id to load next via summer_read_library.
use_when: the first move for any task, before building anything — find the entry that covers what the user asked
not sure which entry (skill, tool, template, reference) applies to the task at hand
narrowing the library to one kind with the kinds filter, or hiding preview entries

resources.summary: Select a node in the editor scene tree and show it in the inspector.
use_when: focusing the user's editor on a specific node
highlighting the player in the scene tree so the user can see it
showing the user the node whose properties are about to change

resources.summary: Set a node property using Godot string syntax for vectors, colors, transforms, and resource class names.
use_when: configuring nodes after adding them
"move the light up" / "put the player at the spawn point" / "make the sprite red" / "rotate the camera 45 degrees"
setting one node's position, rotation, scale, colour, speed, collision layer, or visible flag

resources.summary: Set a nested property on a resource attached to a node, like a collision shape size or material color.
use_when: modifying sub-properties of meshes, materials, or shapes
"make the box mesh 2 metres wide" / "change the capsule radius"
setting the material albedo colour or roughness on a mesh

resources.summary: Detect and crop every distinct game asset from a generated sheet image, uploading named slices with bounding boxes.
use_when: splitting a generated asset or UI sheet into individually usable assets
"cut the generated icon sheet into separate PNGs"
"I have one image with 12 props on it, make them individual assets"

resources.summary: Move one 3D subject along a world ray until it sits at the requested gap from the first surface (floor, ramp, shelf, table), then save the scene.
use_when: seating a prop on a floor, ramp, table, or shelf instead of hand-tuning its Y position
grounding an imported or instantiated model that floats or sinks into its support

resources.summary: Diff two world snapshots into added/removed/changed nodes and count deltas — the structural receipt that a mutation did exactly what was intended.
use_when: verifying a mutation batch against the snapshot_id taken before it
"what changed in the scene after that script ran?"
proving a batch only moved the props it was meant to

resources.summary: Read-only 3D placement rundown for one node — 26 directional clearance casts, contact-or-overlap evidence, grounding, nearby geometry. Never moves or saves.
use_when: learning what surrounds a placed prop before and after a correction — which direction is blocked, by what, and at what distance
diagnosing an overlap or a floating object when summer_test_placement reports fits false or grounded false and you need to know which side to move
checking wall gaps, shelf support, or alcove clearance for a rotated subject (directionSpace local)

resources.summary: Plan the right Summer workflow for a game-building task: skill routes, tool groups, confirmation gates, and verification steps.
use_when: starting any substantial AI game-building task, before mutating the project
the user asks for a whole feature (inventory, boss fight, day-night cycle) and the path is not obvious
choosing which skills and confirmation gates apply before touching the project

resources.summary: Stop the running game (or one named offscreen instance). Does not revert scene edits, undo anything, or save — the editor state is left exactly as it is.
use_when: runtime verification is finished
the game must restart to pick up scene or script changes
a runaway or frozen playtest needs killing
an offscreen playtest instance (summer_play with instance + mode offscreen) is no longer needed — pass instance

resources.summary: Ghost-test one 3D node at a candidate global pose without moving it — overlap evidence, grounded state, signed floor gap. Read-only.
use_when: deciding whether a prop fits in a shelf, cubby, doorway, platform, or dense set before committing the transform
re-checking a saved pose after snap or align to confirm it still clears its neighbours

resources.summary: List the editor's named actions or invoke one by name exactly as its menu item / shortcut would — open Project Settings, switch screens, toggle panels.
use_when: "open project settings in the editor" / "open the Import dock" / "toggle the animation bottom panel" — an editor-workflow step a human would do with the mouse, driven by its stable action name
finding the exact action name (mode list, filter) before invoking it, and reading which names are denied
a step has no dedicated tool (summer_open_scene, summer_select_node, summer_save_scene) but the editor has a menu item or shortcut for it

resources.summary: Activate one editor control by tree path — press, toggle, focus, select a tab, type text, dial a value — or dismiss a blocking dialog; state is read back.
use_when: "dismiss the dialog that is blocking the editor" / "close that popup" — action dismiss_dialog with the path or title from summer_ui_tree root dialogs
"switch the editor to the 3D view" / "go to the Script screen" — path main_screen, action select_tab, value 3D
pressing a button, selecting a tab, typing into a search field, or dialling a slider that no named action covers, using a path from summer_ui_tree

resources.summary: PNG of the editor window or one dock/dialog/control as an image — the pixels-last fallback for looking at the editor UI, never for picking click coordinates.
use_when: "show me what the editor looks like right now" / "screenshot the Inspector dock" — seeing layout or an unfamiliar panel after summer_ui_tree has described it
sanity-checking an editor-UI step visually when the structured read-back is not enough

resources.summary: Structured tree of the live editor UI (controls, paths, text, state) or every visible dialog with its blocking flag — the cheap alternative to a screenshot.
use_when: "is a dialog blocking the editor" / "what does the Inspector dock show" / "which main screen is active" — read editor UI state as structure instead of pixels
finding a control's path before summer_ui_activate, and reading its state back afterwards
listing visible dialogs and popups (root dialogs) before dismissing one with summer_ui_activate action dismiss_dialog

resources.summary: Wait for an engine event — the game starting, an op finishing, a script error, a save — instead of sleeping and re-polling; honest timeout.
use_when: "wait for the game to start" — right after summer_play, wait for play.started instead of guessing how long boot takes
"wait for an event" / "tell me when the import finishes" — block on op.applied / op.failed for one requestId, import.completed, or scene.saved after a long op
during a playtest, catching script.error the moment it fires instead of reading the console afterwards
any time you would otherwise sleep and re-check state — take a cursor with summer_recent_events first, then wait from it

resources.summary: Compact structured snapshot of the edited scene (paths, transforms, world AABBs, fingerprints, counts) — the cheap read before and after every mutation batch.
use_when: taking a diffable baseline before a mutation batch, or verifying transforms/AABBs/fingerprints after one
"where exactly is everything in this scene?" — positions, sizes, bounds
"are these two props overlapping?" / "is anything floating?"

resources.summary: Create or safely overwrite one complete text file through the identity-bound engine; exactly one guard is required, so writes fail closed.
use_when: creating a new project file with the create-only guard
overwriting an existing file with its sha256 receipt
